notes: Reasonable early HQ pressure, but from turn 16 on the Runner only clicked for credits up to 29 and never contested Server 1 while the Corp advanced and scored its last two agendas there.

Against a Runner that never ran, the Corp scored behind ice but very slowly, with many credit clicks at 9-15 credits, odd La Costa Grid counters on itself and a Server 2 card advanced repeatedly and never scored.
After a promising turn 8 the Runner let Paladin Poemu trash its only breaker and then clicked for credits to 64 for over ten turns, never installing anything or pressuring the Corp's scoring remotes.

The Corp sat at 0-3 credits for most of the game while holding Hedge Fund, using Sprint and draws instead of clicking up to cast it, so HQ ice stayed unrezzed and the Runner ran HQ four times a turn, stealing Project Ingatan; it won only thanks to Mélies and late campaigns.
Strong, fast R&D and remote pressure won on turn 5; the only oddity was Window of Opportunity derezzing an ice the Corp rezzed again for 1.

From turn 8 the Corp only clicked for credits, reaching 48 and discarding every turn, and never installed an agenda in its four-ice remote, so the Runner stole the agendas piled up in HQ behind a single Eli.
Efficient aggressive play with timely HQ and remote runs, using Nanuq, Gauss and paying through Grubber to win on turn 7, though it left tags floating.

The Runner bounced off the same rezzed Afshar on HQ nine times, losing 2 credits each time, then clicked for credits to 35 for many turns and never contested the remote where the Corp scored its final agendas.

The Corp's economy stayed at 0-5 credits throughout, and its Longevity Serum use trashed its entire hand, including agendas, into an unprotected Archives, where the Runner stole the winning Regenesis.

A tight, low-credit Jinteki game of fast advancing, Bladderwort and Anemone grinding that won on turn 13; it took a risk with a naked remote Hybrid Release and lost See How They Run from an unrezzed HQ.
Scored steadily behind ice against a passive Runner, but several turns were spent clicking for credits while discarding from a clogged hand, and the win took 15 turns.
Sensible R&D pressure through Ballista, but the economy was chronically thin and the grip went unused, it could not contest the scoring remote, and an underfunded third R&D run lost Boi-tatá.
The Corp spent repeated clicks and nearly all its credits trashing resources while three agendas sat in a weakly defended HQ and were stolen; it installed nothing to score until it was too late.

Good early R&D runs stole Yagi-Uda, but against a Jinteki deck that had just dealt 3 net damage, it ended turn 6 with one card in grip while an advanced remote sat unchecked, and was flatlined by Fujii Asset Retrieval.
Solid multi-access HQ and R&D pressure with Docklands Pass and Shibboleth won on turn 14; the one misstep was running into the known Karunā a second time for 2 more net damage.
The Corp kept installing agendas into the same remote protected only by Eli and a non-ETR Wave, which the Runner had already broken, and lost four agendas there while sitting at 0-4 credits.
Aggressive and effective, taking agendas from HQ through Ballista and using Banner to push through a three-ice remote for the turn-10 win.
Stuck at 0-4 credits clicking for credits, the Corp fired Neurospike for no effect and left three Sericulture Expansions on cheap-to-break Diviner/Hafrún servers or in HQ, all of which were stolen.
It built a strong taxing HQ wall and good campaign economy, then scored remotes with Seamless Launch and an ADT-revealed Ingatan, though that Ingatan sat naked for two turns.
After an early steal, the Runner clicked for credits to 69 for a dozen turns, never contested the Corp's advancing remotes and even let a 1-credit Paywall end its run while holding over 60 credits.
